subject: Variance explained discrepancies between formula and fitqtl

messages.author: 25e13e522040f0b9
messages.subject: Variance explained discrepancies between formula and fitqtl
parts:
Hi Karl,

I get 6.4% variance explained using 1 - 10^(-(2/n)*LOD), but only 2.3% using fitqtl with formula=y~Q1
What is the nature of the discrepancy?

If I use refineqtl the LOD increases by 0.6 but variance explained after fitqtl decreases to 1.5%.

In relationship to this issue, if I have two unlinked QTL, I would have assumed that % variance explained using fitqtl with formula=y~Q1+Q2 would be better than adding the result of each QTL with 1 - 10^(-(2/n)*LOD) but I'm still struggling with the difference between the two methods for calculating variance explained.

Thanks for your help,

Andrés

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Variance explained discrepancies between formula and fitqtl
parts:
fitqtl calculates the variance explained from the LOD score using that same formula. 
Are the LOD scores the same? Are you using the same fitting method (eg Haley-Knott regression)?

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Variance explained discrepancies between formula and fitqtl
parts:
The LOD scores from fitqtl are much lower (2.1) than from scanone (6.7), using hk for both.
Interestingly, even though I specify method="hk" in fitqtl, the summary says it is using multiple imputation.

out.fq <- fitqtl(cross, pheno.col=1, qtl=qtl, formula=y~Q1, method="hk")
summary(out.fq)


out <- scanone(cross, pheno.col=1, model="normal", method="hk")
summary(out)


Chromosome 4 is the one that went into makeqtl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Variance explained discrepancies between formula and fitqtl
parts:
Hi Karl,

I discovered the problem: It was at the makeqtl step. If I use the genotype probabilities, and not the imputed genotypes, I get the same result from fitqtl as I get from 1 - 10^(-(2/n)*LOD). 
Lessoned learned.

Thanks for taking the time to help so quickly.

Andrés
